components.title: GSA Common Controls
components.description: This Common Control Catalog (CCC) was developed in order to provide stakeholders with the detailed information on what GSA considers inheritable common controls and who the responsible party is for implementing the control.
components.purpose: The purpose of this guide is to provide direction on the NIST SP 800-53 controls where GSA’s IT security and privacy programs provide a policy, procedure, process, or capability meeting all or part of a control requirement. This guide provides each control’s implementation status, control type (i.e., common, hybrid, system specific), details on the control implementation, and any system expectations for both Federal and Vendor/Contractor systems.

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Common controls are controls whose implementation results in a capability that is inheritable by multiple systems or programs.

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Organizations can implement a control as hybrid if one part of the control is common (inheritable) and the other part is system specific

control-implementations.description:
Security and privacy controls/enhancements from NIST SP 800-53 included in this plan are either:

  * Common controls - where a GSA organization or program provides the entire control; or
  * Hybrid controls - where a GSA organization or program provides a part of the control.

The implementation guidance provided in this plan is applicable to GSA Federal Employees, contractors, and vendors of GSA, who operate, manage, maintain, and protect GSA systems (Federal and Contractor systems) and information.

implemented-requirements.description:
Inactivity Logout is a policy-based Common Control provided by
[GSA Order CIO 2104.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “GSA Information Technology (IT)
General Rules of Behavior” Category Access - (3) Logoff and shutdown your GSA workstation at the
end of the workday.

Inactivity logout is behavior- or policy-based and requires users to take physical action to log
out when they expect to be inactive longer than a defined period of time. A system’s automatic
enforcement of user inactivity logout is documented by AC-11.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners, ISSOs, and ISSMs must document the terms
and conditions of external system interconnections within a system Interconnection
Security Agreement (ISA). When a system ISA is required, System Owners, ISSOs, and ISSM must review
[GSA Order CIO 2104.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library),
“GSA Information Technology (IT) General Rules of Behavior,” and determine if a system-
specific defined Rules of Behavior (RoB) (see PL-4) is required. If a system specific RoB is
required, the System Owner must ensure the system’s RoB is reflected in the ISA and is
communicated to all personnel who require system access.

statements.description:
1. New GSA personnel (i.e., contractors and federal employees) must read and acknowledge
[GSA Order CIO 2104.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “GSA Information Technology (IT)
General Rules of Behavior,” within 90 days of receiving their Enterprise Network Account
(i.e., Long Name Account). After this, they must complete the GSA IT Security and Privacy
Awareness curriculum annually.
1. GSA personnel receive additional communications to raise cybersecurity awareness during the
year. The OCISO and GSA IT communications teams conduct these campaigns in response to
security trends, significant events, and user feedback.

The OCISO Policy and Compliance Division (ISP) coordinates campaigns year-round to raise
cybersecurity awareness. Campaigns include frequent phishing campaigns against different user
groups, including VIPs and Privileged Users; security vignettes via email; and a robust
communications campaign during the annual Cybersecurity Awareness month.

GSA's mandatory IT Security and Privacy Awareness course is updated annually. Updates are based
on an analysis of security-related trends and user feedback

OCISO ISP incorporates insight shared in security incident/breach reports when these reports are
shared with them This insight will contribute to the goals of the training.

describes GSA’s roles, responsibilities, and policy regarding its insider threat program (ITP).
ITP personnel, under the Associate Administrator for Mission Assurance, are
responsible for ensuring insider threat information and training is provided annually at a minimum.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** This control's requirements apply and are satisfied by
the Office of Mission Assurance (OMA) training program for GSA personnel who are provisioned with
an Enterprise Network Account (i.e., ENT Long-Name Account [LNA]) and who manage GSA Federal
systems. Therefore, System Owners can inherit this control entirely to meet these security
training requirements.

OCISO's mandatory Security and Privacy Awareness course supports this control. This course
teaches students

1. how to recognize and report phishing attacks, a form of social engineering
2) how their social media presence could be used against them.

All GSA personnel are required to take this training. Throughout the year,
the OCISO sends security vignettes to reinforce the concepts introduced in this course.

records notices, privacy impact assessments, and other related data management documentation.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners are required to maintain training records
for any system specific role-based training provided to users of the information system.

statements.description:
The OCISO issues AO Designation Letters, per Services/Staff Offices and other organizations
identifying their authorizing official for all GSA information systems.

If a platform or system providing controls for other systems is authorized to operate, any common
controls it is providing are authorized, by the assigned AO per part a.

[GSA Order CIO 2100.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “GSA Information Technology (IT) Security Policy,” and
[CIO-IT-Security 06-30](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Managing Enterprise Cybersecurity Risk require AOs to review and approve security
safeguards of information systems and issue ATO approvals for each information system,
application, or set of common controls under their purview based on the acceptability of the
implementation of security safeguards in place (risk-management approach).

CIO 2100.1 and CIO-IT Security 06-30 state that final authority to operate or not operate an
information system, application, or a set of common controls rests with the AO.

CIO 2100.1 and CIO-IT Security-06-30 require authorizations to be updated in accordance with the
timelines defined in CIO-IT Security-06-30 and GSA’s other A&A process guides. As specified in
CIO-IT Security-06-30, authorizations are updated at least every three years or upon significant
changes. Systems in ongoing authorization undergo biannual performance metric monitoring
which fulfills the update requirement.

implemented-requirements.description:
**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners, ISSOs, and ISSMs are
responsible for monitoring and performing assigned system level metrics in accordance with GSA IT Security
Policies and procedures as defined by CIO-IT Security-06-30, CIO-IT Security-17-80: Vulnerability
Management Process, and CIO-IT Security-12-66: Information Security Continuous Monitoring Strategy.

statements.description:
The GSA OCISO developed [CIO-IT Security-12-66](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Information Security Continuous Monitoring Strategy (ISCM) & Ongoing Authorization (OA) Program
and has established system-level metric monitoring requirements, as defined by
[CIO-IT Security-08-39](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Management Implementation Plan and CIO-IT Security-12-66.

The GSA OCISO has established system-level monitoring and control assessment requirements
within CIO-IT Security-08-39 and CIO-IT Security-12-66.

Systems’ ongoing control assessments are performed based on GSA’s ATO processes defined by
[CIO-IT Security-06-30](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides)
and CIO-IT Security-12-66 for systems accepted into the OA Program.
Additionally, the OCISO requires systems to complete an annual FISMA Self-Assessment unless
they have completed a full assessment in the current FY.

The GSA OCISO performs ongoing monitoring of system and organization-defined metrics using
[automated enterprise management tools and manual processes](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides) defined by:

* CIO-IT Security-06-30: Managing Enterprise Risk
* CIO-IT Security-08-39: Management Implementation Plan
* CIO-IT Security-09-44: Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M)
* CIO-IT Security-17-80: Vulnerability Management Process
* CIO-IT Security-18-91: Risk Management Strategy (RMS)
* CIO-IT Security-19-101: External Information System Monitoring

System Owners, ISSOs, and ISSMs are responsible for monitoring and performing assigned system
level metrics in accordance with GSA IT Security Policies and procedures.

System-assigned ISSOs and ISSMs record and manage the mitigation and remediation of identified
weaknesses and deficiencies, not associated with accepted risks, in organizational information
systems’ POA&M per CIO-IT Security-09-44. System-assigned ISSOs and ISSMs continuously
perform system-level correlation and analysis of assessment results and system risk monitoring
activities by performing POA&M management in coordination with System Owners and system
custodians.

The GSA OCISO performs POA&M reviews upon completion of an A&A and quarterly thereafter.
System Level quarterly POA&M Review Reports are generated by the OCSIO and are provided to
ISSOs for quality reviews and process improvement activities. ISSM Management Reports are
generated quarterly by the OCISO to provide an agency view of status in correcting weaknesses or
deficiencies associated with the managed information system portfolio.

The GSA OCISO has established and defined system-level response action requirements within:

* CIO-IT Security-06-30: Managing Enterprise Cybersecurity Risk
* CIO-IT Security-09-44: Plan of Action and Milestones
* CIO-IT Security-17-80: Vulnerability Management Process

System Owners, ISSOs, and ISSMs are responsible for managing system-level risk response
activities as system risks are identified per monitoring and assessment activities.

The GSA OCISO has established and defined methods for reporting system-level security and
privacy status within CIO-IT Security-08-39 and CIO-IT Security-12-66. The OCISO conducts
quarterly AO/CISO briefings during which systems’ cyber hygiene and operational statuses are
reported to the AOs.

System Owners, ISSOs, ISSMs, and system custodians are responsible for reporting system-level
security and privacy statuses per predefined reporting frequencies and mechanisms (e.g., ISSO
Checklists, POA&Ms, and ad hoc data calls).

implemented-requirements.description:
The OCISO Policy and Compliance Division (ISP) performs operational oversight of the
agency’s Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) strategy and Ongoing
Authorization (OA) Program. ISP performs assessment activities of the information
systems accepted into the OA Program, per the program’s monitoring
and reporting requirements and with impartiality.

The OCISO has established [CIO-IT Security-12-66](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Information Security Continuous Monitoring Strategy (ISCM) & Ongoing Authorization (OA) Program
that includes effective compliance and risk monitoring policies and procedures defined by
[CIO-IT Security-06-30](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Managing Enterprise Cybersecurity Risk. The guidance establishes the agency’s assessment,
authorization, and monitoring requirements for each managed GSA information system.
The procedural requirements define the continuous monitoring of system controls and relevant
documents, or records created by the agency in performing lifecycle management activities; Security
Assessment Reports (SAPs), Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), Security, System Security
and Privacy Plans (SSPPs), and System Assessment Reports (SAR).

For systems in scope per the defined parameter, the GSA OCISO PEN Testing team can provide penetration
testing in support of GSA information systems’ A&A activities and annually per testing requirements defined by
CIO-IT Security-06-30: Managing Enterprise Cybersecurity Risk and CIO-IT Security-11-51: Conducting
Penetration Test Exercises. If the GSA OCISO PEN Testing team is used:

* This control becomes hybrid between the GSA OCISO PEN Testing team and the system.
* A Penetration Test Rules of Engagement (RoE) is documented prior to starting testing activities to
minimize the potential for service disruptions, damage, or loss of system integrity. The RoE outlines the
responsibilities and limitations of the GSA OCISO PEN Testing team and system personnel throughout
the testing processes.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** For systems that do not have an applicable
penetration testing requirement, control CA-8 must be documented as not required in the system’s CA-8
control response.

If the GSA OCISO PEN Testing team performs a system’s penetration testing, the System Owner, ISSO, and ISSM
must coordinate with the OCISO PEN Testing team’s penetration testing services.

AOs/System Owners may elect to contract an external penetration testing vendor for meeting their system’s
penetration testing requirements, making the control system specific. The third party must complete the
minimum requirements set forth by CIO-IT Security-11-51. If the penetration testing is performed by an external
vendor, the resultant report must reflect the external vendor penetration testing of the system boundary.

values: all Internet accessible, FIPS 199 High impact, and High Value Asset (HVA) information systems

implemented-requirements.description:
The GSA OCISO Penetration Testing Team performs penetration testing activities on behalf of GSA as an
independent testing agent. The GSA PEN Testing team is free from any perceived or actual conflicts of interest
with respect to the development, operation, or management of the systems that are the targets of the
penetration testing activities performed by the team.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners, ISSOs, and ISSMs must ensure
assigned systems’ penetration testing requirements are met. If the system’s penetration testing is performed by
the OCISO PEN Testing team, CA-8(1) is a Common Control provided by the OCSIO. If penetration testing is
performed by an external vendor, independence must be documented and accepted. Independence is waived
for all annual testing (i.e., testing can be internally performed).

statements.description:
GSA has implemented an agency-wide incident response program with formal policies, procedural
guidelines, and supporting processes managed by the OCISO. The Incident Handling control
requirements are implemented as a hybrid control with each GSA managed information system per
the Incident Response processes, documented by
[CIO-IT Security-01-02](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Incident Response (IR) also known as the “GSA IR Plan.”

System Owners are responsible for ensuring assigned systems are aligned with either a system-
specific or Service Staff Office (SSO) Tier 1 and 2 Incident Response Plan that is aligned with
Incident Handling and Reporting requirements in CIO-IT Security-01-02.

The GSA IR Plan is consistent with
[NIST SP 800-61 Revision 2](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-61r2.pdf),
“Computer Security Incident Handling Guide.” The supporting incident response process is performed
on a “Tiered” basis, including Tier 1 through Tier 3, and is fully defined in section 4 of
CIO-IT Security-01-02. Key tasks in the Tiers are summarized below:

* Tier 1 – Observe event/incident, open ticket in ServiceNow, provide data to IR Team, and
stabilize the system.
* Tier 2 – Determine seriousness of threat, verify notification and reporting, coordinate with
Tier 1, collect data, isolate systems as necessary, support Tier 3, and remediate and restore.
* Tier 3 – Direct data collection, lead response team, conduct detailed technical analysis,
prepare, and submit reports.

For serious incidents or those in which problems in response were identified; an OCISO Lessons
Learned meeting is conducted where the incident is reviewed to identify necessary improvements
including people, process, and technology.

The OCSIO Incident Response Team, in coordination with the CISO, regularly reviews GSA’s Incident
Handling activities performed throughout the incident period. Process improvements and
identification of inefficiencies in the agency’s incident detection, handling, and reporting is
performed continuously.

implemented-requirements.description:
All incident information generated as part of response activities is maintained by the Incident
Response Team in ServiceNow. Additional automated mechanisms supporting GSA’s incident handling
processes include:

**Incident Handling Tools:**

The GSA Incident Response Team utilizes several automated tools and services that are used to assist
in incident handling, including:

* _Enterprise Logging Platform_ - The SIEM Tool that collects and correlates event log data from network devices across the network, including Firewalls, IDP/IPS devices, Web Proxies, and Wireless Access Points.
* _FireEye Endpoint Security (HX series)_ - An endpoint-based solution that allows security analysts to conduct detailed investigations to identify and contain Indicators of Compromise (IOC) related to APT malware.
* _Bit9_ - Deployed as an application whitelisting solution that identifies executables on GSA workstations/servers in a central repository for investigation into whether malware was executed on a device.
* _Palo Alto Wildfire_ - Cloud-based malware detection service which performs static and dynamic analysis of binary executables ingressing the GSA network. Alerts on detection of malware.
* _MaaS360_ - Software management tool that GSA uses to deploy and inventory software on workstations and mobile devices.
* _FireEye Managed Defense Portal_ - Allows for access to alerts from FireEye regarding threats.
* _CenturyLink Portal_ - Allows for access to alerts from the CenturyLink Security Operations Center.
* _FireEye Intelligence_ - Allows for access to FireEye (formerly iSIGHT Partners) Vulnerability and Threat Reports.

**Forensic Tool Sources:**

GSA OCISO uses a combination of commercial and open-source tools to capture cyber-forensic evidence
as part of a Tier 3 investigation. Detailed forensics investigations are also supported by several
additional commercial off the shelf (COTS) and open-source tools, including, but not limited to,
the following:

* Mobile Forensics Tools
* _Katana Forensics Lantern_ - Allows image acquisition for mobile devices, specializing in iOS.
* _viaForensics viaExtract_ - Provides forensic capabilities for Android devices, including image acquisition.
* General Forensics
* _FTK Forensic Toolkit_ - Provides the ability to conduct detailed forensic investigations on various platforms, such as hard drives, mobile devices, network data, and internet storage.
* _EnCase Forensic Imager_ - Provides the ability to acquire forensic images from local disks.
* Live Response Forensics
* _FireEye Memoryze_ - Provides ability to acquire and/or analyze memory images, and on live systems, can include the paging file in its analysis.

The OCISO manages the GSA Incident Response Team, which is responsible for tracking all security
incidents for GSA IT systems (including vendor-owned and -operated systems) reported to the OCISO.
Incident reports include (as applicable) the status of the incident and any pertinent information
gathered as part of the overall response process, including but not limited to vulnerability
details, system information, and forensics evidence.

Incident information generated as part of response activities is maintained in ServiceNow and
centrally managed by the Incident Response Team, which coordinates the overall response
including required reporting to United States Computer Emergency Readiness Team (US-CERT).

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners, ISSOs, ISSMs, and system
custodians are responsible for reporting incidents in accordance with CIO-IT Security-01-02.

statements.description:
GSA has implemented an agency-wide incident response program with formal policies, procedural
guidelines, and supporting processes managed by the OCISO Security Operations Division (ISO).
Incident Reporting is implemented as hybrid security control with each GSA managed information
system per the Incident Response processes, including “How to Report IT Security Incidents” as
documented in
[CIO-IT Security-01-02](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): Incident Response (IR).

The OCISO follows the United States Computer Emergency Readiness Team (US-CERT) Federal
Incident Reporting Guidelines. These guidelines require agencies to report information security
incidents, in which the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of a federal information system
of a civilian Executive Branch agency is potentially compromised, to the National Cybersecurity and
Communications Integration Center/US-CERT with the required data elements, as well as any other
available information, within one hour of being identified by the agency’s top-level Computer
Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT), Security Operations Center (SOC), or information
technology department.

Time is critical. GSA personnel are advised to report incidents to the GSA IT Service Desk immediately
upon incident identification. After normal business hours, on-call IR support is available
at 202-501-0980 and the GSA Incident Response team can also be contacted at gsa-ir@gsa.gov. If there
is no immediate response during business hours, contact the SecOps on-call personnel.

implemented-requirements.description:
All GSA IT security incidents are to be reported to the GSA OCISO consistent with the reporting
requirements described in
[CIO-IT Security-01-02](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): Incident Response (IR).

The OCISO provides incident response coordination for all incidents involving GSA systems by
leveraging GSA’s automated ticketing system ServiceNow. The first line of support is provided by
the GSA IT Service Desk when an incident is reported and then documented within a ServiceNow incident
ticket. ServiceNow IR tickets are distributed to OCISO Incident Response personnel to initiate
incident response and coordinate incident communications. OCISO staff can open ServiceNow IR incident
tickets upon discovery or upon receiving a report of an incident.

The GSA OCISO has established a Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) Program within the
Identity, Credential, Access Management (ICAM) Shared Services Division (ISI) for any IT security
incident that involves a potential compromise of the supply chain for a provider of a product or
service utilized by GSA. The incident information is forwarded to the Shared Services Division (ISI)
(isi-federal@gsa.gov). ISI coordinates with the Incident Response Team and ensures all relevant
incident information is shared with entities within or outside of GSA, as required.

The GSA OCSIO Incident Response Team provides Tier 3 support in response to reported security
incidents as a common IT Security support service to all GSA managed systems. The first line of
support is provided through the GSA IT Service Desk when an incident is initially reported.

The GSA OCISO staffs a 24x7x365 Security Operations Center (SOC) that provides Incident Response (IR)
support for Tier 3 incident handling. The OCISO Tier 3 Response Team is trained in Security Incident
Response and Forensic Investigation services. The Tier 3 Response Team coordinates all agency
incident response investigations with the affected System Owner, ISSO, ISSM, and designated system
custodians throughout the investigation and response period of the incident. The Tier 3 Response Team
approves all remedial and return to service actions in consultation with the OCISO. Additional System
Owner and end user incident response assistance is provided by the OCISO on a case-by-case basis.

All IT security incidents are to be reported to the GSA OCISO consistent with the reporting
requirements described within
[CIO-IT Security-01-02](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):

GSA IT systems regardless of ownership (internal or external) with GSA management, United States
Computer Emergency Readiness Team (US-CERT), external law enforcement, and the GSA Inspector General.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners are responsible for providing
system supporting resources during an Incident Response investigation when needed.

All GSA IT security incidents are to be reported to the GSA OCISO consistent with the reporting

The inventory data is made available to the GSA Incident Response Team for coordinating
communications per systems affected by a security threat or incident. Additionally, the GSA Incident
Response Team can submit GSA IR data to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS)/CISO leveraging
ServiceNow reporting capabilities and for requesting additional incident support if needed.

requirements to GSA consistent with CIO-IT Security-01-02. Each may be covered by a GSA Service and
