System Owners are responsible for ensuring all security architecture changes are reflected in their
System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP), Concept of Operations (CONOPS), criticality analysis, and
organizational procedures and procurements/acquisitions (as applicable and/or annually, as part of
the system’s annual SSPP review/update processing).

implemented-requirements.description:
The GSA OCISO and Privacy Office provide the Central Management control requirement as a Common Control
to all GSA managed information systems that leverage GSA IT management services. The centrally managed GSA
IT common and hybrid security and privacy controls are communicated and documented by
[CIO-IT Security-Privacy-18-90](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): Common Control Catalog (CCC).

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners, ISSOs, and ISSMs are to leverage
the common and hybrid security and privacy controls documented within CIO-IT Security-Privacy-18-90 when
performing Baseline Tailoring of their System Security and Privacy Plans (SSPP).

A system’s FIPS 199 security categorization and Privacy Threshold Analysis (PTA) determines the initial set of
NIST SP 800-53 control requirements an information system must implement. GSA’s baseline selection process,
“Identifying Appropriate ATU or ATO Process” is defined within [CIO-IT Security-06-30](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): Managing Enterprise Cybersecurity Risk.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners, Data Owners, ISSOs, and ISSMs
must first document the system’s FIPS 199 and PTA prior to the baseline selection determination. The System
Owner collaborates with the AO, ISSM, ISSO, and Privacy Team as necessary to complete the control baseline
selection.

Once the security control baseline for a system is selected, tailoring of those controls commences. A system’s
Baseline Tailoring tasks include:

* Determining the common controls the system inherits;
* Assigning values to any parameters identified as being left up to the system for assignment and
requiring GSA AO and CISO approval;
* Determining if any compensating or supplemental controls are required to address unique
organizational and/or system specific needs. These needs may be based on a risk assessment (either
formal or informal), local conditions including environment of operation, organization-specific security
requirements, specific threat information, cost-benefit analyses, or special circumstances.

System specific justifications or rationale for tailoring actions is required, especially where the CISO and AO
must approve assignments and if any controls are identified as not applicable to the system or its environment.

System teams must complete a [Control Tailoring Workbook](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13uwvTJY06LPzNutWYzId7BV-3dmWya8fM-4aGmYP0vA/edit?usp=share_link) (CTW) and provide it as an attachment to the SSPP.
The CTW identifies the GSA defined values for [NIST SP 800-53](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-53r5.pdf) control assignments and selections. The selected
security controls, including all controls or enhancements selected above the baseline for the information
system, are documented in the SSPP. Both the SSPP and the CTW identify parameter assignments or selections
deferred to the SSO or contractor for recommendation and approval by the GSA AO and CISO. The CTW
contains columns for identifying the defined values and GSA approval of the values.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners are to collaborate with the ISSM,
ISSO, Privacy Team as necessary, and other System Owners (regarding common/hybrid controls) to complete
their assigned system’s control tailoring requirements.

statements.description:
The OCISO developed CIO-IT Security-Privacy-18-90: Common Control Catalog (CCC) to address the
following requirements. The CCC is disseminated GSA-wide via GSA’s InSite centralized agency
[IT Security Procedural Guides website](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides).

1. GSA’s CCC provides implementation details or refers to a separate system/capability that
provides the details, for common and hybrid controls, including program management controls,
provided at the enterprise level.
2. The roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational
entities, and compliance for the common and hybrid controls with an enterprise component are
either defined in the procedural guide referenced in the control’s “-1” control or included in the
implementation details of the referenced guide or the control implementation.
3. The control implementation details are coordinated with other organizational entities
responsible for them either as part of the development of the CCC or development of the
various procedural guides referred to in the “-1” controls for each control family.
4. The plan is approved by the CISO and is designed to give clear direction as to which GSA division
or organization is responsible for implementation of the control.

The GSA OCISO is responsible for reviewing and updating CIO-IT Security-Privacy-18-90 every three
years and following changes to Federal or GSA policies, requirements, or guidance.

This guide is only disseminated GSA-wide via GSA’s InSite centralized agency
[IT Security Procedural Guides website](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides).
It is protected from modification by being a signed PDF document, any editing of the
document would void the signature.

implemented-requirements.description:
GSA has an appointed Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), who provides oversight and resources for
developing, implementing, and maintaining GSA’s enterprise-wide information security program. The GSA CISO
manages and oversees the operation of the five Offices of the Chief Information Security Officer (OCISO)
divisions: Security Engineering (ISE), Security Operations (ISO), Policy and Compliance (ISP), Identity, Credential
and Access Management (ICAM) Shared Services (ISI), and Information System Security Officer (ISSO) Support
(IST).

statements.description:
IT security costs and resources are a part of the internal annual budget process for review and
approval as part of the GSA Enterprise IT Governance process, including the GSA Investment Review
Board (IRB).

GSA annually submits Exhibit 53A for reporting all the GSA IT security costs and resources managed
by OCISO, and privacy costs and resources managed by the Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP).

The GSA IT Governance process and IRB ensure that all investments include security and privacy
resources.

1. The GSA process for implementing Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) is documented in
[GSA Order CIO 2100.1](https://www.gsa.gov/directives-library),
“GSA Information Technology (IT) Security Policy,”
[CIO-IT Security-09-44](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M), and
[CIO-IT Security-06-30](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Managing Enterprise Cybersecurity Risk.
2. CIO-IT Security-09-44 and Security-06-30 document the requirements to remediate risks
associated with GSA’s information systems and GSA’s overall information security program.
3. The GSA OCISO ISP Division collects data on POA&Ms, performs quarterly reviews, and reports
to OCSIO leadership quarterly.

The GSA OCISO ISP Division reviews POA&Ms quarterly and coordinates reviews with the ISSOs and
ISSMs. The reviews are focused on ensuring POA&Ms are accurately documented, and progress is
made on resolving POA&M items in line with agency-wide priorities and risk tolerance. The ISP
Division prepares status reports of its reviews and provides those reports to ISSOs, ISSMs, the CISO,
and AOs and System Owners, as required. Outstanding and delayed POA&M items associated with
signed and approved Acceptance of Risk (AORs) are discussed with AOs on a quarterly basis during
AO sync meetings.

implemented-requirements.description:
The OCISO manages an up-to-date inventory of system inventory data within the GSA System Inventory hosted
by its implementation of Archer Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC). Read-Only inventory data is
replicated to GSA’s EA Analytics and Reporting (GEAR) site and made available for internal GSA usage. Inventory
data managed for each information system includes, but is not limited to the following attributes:

* System Name
* System Alias/Acronym
* FISMA System Identifier/Tag
* Responsible IT Organization
* Federal or Contractor Designation
* FIPS 199 Impact level
* Authority-to-Operate (ATO) Type
* ATO Date
* ATO Renewal Date
* Contains Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
* Cloud Hosted

The GSA OCISO and the GSA Privacy Office leverage the Archer GRC Agency System Inventory for maintaining an
up-to-date inventory of GSA information systems, applications, and/or projects that process Personally
Identifiable Information (PII). The GSA Privacy Office annually validates that the Agency System Inventory
properly reflects all systems, applications and/or projects that process PII data. GSA FISMA systems that process
PII are reflected in GEAR with an attribute of “Contains PII” for easy reporting.

The GSA leadership team develops Information Security and Privacy Performance measures for each Fiscal year.
These performance metrics are aligned with the GSA IT goals to operate efficiently, to deliver business value, to
lead IT innovation across the Federal Government, and to continue to transform GSA IT. Performance metrics
for each fiscal year are also influenced by external Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and Department of
Homeland Security (DHS) reporting requirements and Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA)
metrics. The IS and ID performance metric progress and accomplishments are required to be reported to GSA
leadership on a quarterly basis.

GSA also provides security and privacy performance progress updates on GSA’s Information Security and Privacy
Programs by responding to periodic OMB and DHS data calls. GSA currently provides responses to quarterly and
annual FISMA metrics, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Binding Operational Directives
(BOD) and Emergency Directives (EDs), data calls and reporting within CyberScope, and reporting as required for
actions within OMB Memorandums.

GSA’s Office of Enterprise Planning and Governance (IDR) in GSA IT is responsible for GSA’s enterprise
architecture and for:

* Developing and maintaining GSA’s current (As-Is) and target (To-Be) architecture and working with GSA
business units to develop segment and solution architecture plans.
* Developing the IT service strategy, design, and transition planning.
* Developing and implementing IT Policy.

[GSA Order CIO 2160.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “GSA Information Technology (IT) Standards Profile” ensures GSA acquisitions and use of
information technology adhere to the IT Standards Profile. The IT Standards Profile is the official GSA repository
of all approved software applications. It is managed by GSA IT and can be found at [ea.gsa.gov](https://ea.gsa.gov/#!/itstandards).

[GSA Order CIO 2110.4](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “GSA Enterprise Architecture Policy” utilizes GSA’s strategic goals, mission and support
services, data, and enabling technologies to communicate the business vision and target architecture in
conjunction with the GSA Performance Management, Capital Planning, and Investment Control (CPIC), and
Solutions Life Cycle (SLC) processes.

The GSA Enterprise Architecture follows GSA’s SLC methodology, which ensures holistic security, including
enterprise architecture and governance, is incorporated into the system from inception rather than retrofitted
after the fact.

The following are security integration points with Enterprise Architecture:

* Providing a common repository for application and FISMA inventory management
* Reviewing of system architectures to ensure security compliance
* Facilitating all testing needed for initial ATO and periodic reauthorizations
* Providing on-request security consulting

The Privacy Office and Security Engineering Division (ISE) in OCISO works closely with IDR and other Service and
Staff Offices to facilitate integration of security standards/requirements into development efforts, ensuring
secure outcomes as a matter of routine. Information Technology contracts are reviewed by the OCISO and
Privacy Office before release to the public. System architectures are reviewed and approved as part of the ATO
process. Architecture reviews are performed to ensure alignment of system architecture with current and to be
enterprise architecture, meets requirements for critical controls (“show-stopper” controls) and adopts overall
philosophy/approach for cyber security best practices and cyber hygiene.
The offloading of non-essential GSA Enterprise Architecture functions or services has not been implemented.
A critical infrastructure plan has not been implemented.

statements.description:
1. [CIO-IT Security-18-91](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): Risk Management Strategy (RMS) provides a comprehensive approach for
managing risks associated with GSA information systems in accordance with Federal laws,
regulations, and requirements.
2. [CIO-IT Privacy-23-01](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/security-and-privacy/privacy): Privacy Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Processing and
Transparency (PT) provides a comprehensive approach for managing privacy risks associated
with GSA information systems that contain PII data in accordance with Federal laws, regulations,
and requirements.

CIO-IT Security-18-91 establishes an integrated, comprehensive approach to identify, measure, and
manage risk to GSA operations, assets, and individuals associated with the operation and use of GSA
information systems.

The GSA OCISO is responsible for reviewing and updating CIO-IT Security-18-91 biennially.
The GSA Privacy Office is responsible for reviewing and updating CIO-IT Privacy-23-01 biennially.

The GSA OCISO IST and ISP Divisions manage the security and privacy state of all GSA information
systems using the security authorization processes described in
[GSA Order CIO 2100.1](https://www.gsa.gov/directives-library),
“GSA Information Technology (IT) Security Policy” and
[CIO-IT Security-06-30](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Managing Enterprise Cybersecurity Risk and other authorization process guides identified therein.

[CIO-IT Security-18-91](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Risk Management Strategy (RMS), CIO 2100.1, and CIO-IT Security-06-30, designate individual roles and responsibilities within the organizational risk management process.

CIO-IT Security-18-91 and CIO-IT Security-06-30 describe how GSA’s security authorization processes
are integrated into GSA’s risk management program.

All GSA Service and Staff Offices (SSOs) have a defined mission. Each SSO further defines business
processes supporting the SSO mission. [GSA Order CIO 2100.1](https://www.gsa.gov/directives-library), “GSA Information Technology (IT)
Security Policy” and [CIO-IT Security-06-30](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): Managing Enterprise Cybersecurity Risk and other
authorization process guides identified therein, require information security and privacy to be
considered as information systems are used to support GSA’s missions and business processes.
Additionally, GSA has defined 16 Mission Essential functions (MEFs) and Essential Supporting
Activities (ESAs) across GSA SSOs. More information on GSA MEFs is available in
[GSA Order ADM 2430.2](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “The U.S. General Services Administration Continuity of Operations Mission Essential
Functions.”

As part of the processes described in CIO-IT Security-06-30, the mission/business process of systems
is documented in System Security and Privacy Plans (SSPPs). Included within SSPPs is the FIPS 199
security categorization of the system, which along with the specific A&A process the system is
following, results in a set of security and privacy controls required to achieve the system’s protection
needs.

The GSA Office of Mission Assurance (OMA), per ADM 2430.2, reviews GSA Mission Essential
Functions (MEF) and Primary Mission Essential Functions (PMEF) on a biennial basis.
Correspondingly, GSA information systems supporting these MEFs are also updated.

implemented-requirements.description:
[GSA Order ADM 2400.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “Insider Threat Program,” establishes the roles and responsibilities across SSOs to
prevent, deter, detect, and mitigate actions by insiders. The order further identifies the responsibilities to
gather, integrate, centrally analyze, and respond appropriately to insider threats and incidents. As appropriate,
consultation is conducted with records management, legal counsel, civil liberties, and privacy officials to ensure
legal, privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties issues (including, but not limited to, the use of personally identifiable
information) are appropriately addressed.

[CIO-IT Security-05-29](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Security and Privacy Awareness and Role Based Training Program identifies information
security roles within the workforce that require specific role-based security training to further their professional
development. GSA’s OCISO ISP Division also provides role-based training, as required, on emerging topics or
technology that help employees in those roles perform their job functions better. [GSA Order HRM 9410.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides),
“GSA Workforce Learning and Development Policy,” requires all GSA employees to have and maintain up-to-date
Individual Development Plans. Additionally, GSA’s OCISO ISP holds monthly Security Exchange meetings to
evangelize security and discuss challenges and opportunities, and to provide security relevant training to
individuals within and outside of OCISO.

statements.description:
1. The five Office of the Chief Information Security Officer (OCISO) Divisions--Security Engineering
(ISE); Security Operations (ISO); Policy and Compliance (ISP); Information System Security Officer
(ISSO) Support (IST), and Identity, Credential, Access Management (ICAM) Shared Services
Division (ISI)--provide:

* Security testing support for assessing GSA systems.
* Training for various internal GSA processes including but not limited to assessment and authorization processes, Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) management, continuous monitoring, vulnerability scanning, and incident response.
* Monitoring of GSA systems for those same processes (e.g., monitoring Assessment and Authorization (A&A) status and POA&Ms are maintained, monitoring vulnerabilities through scanning, monitoring systems/activities for incidents.)

1. The OCISO divisions provide the activities described above continuously throughout the year and
throughout information systems’ lifecycles.

As part of the scheduled revisions of CIO-IT Security Procedural and Technical guides, all testing,
training, and monitoring guidance, activities, and templates are reviewed and updated to align with
GSA’s risk management strategy and priorities.

The GSA OCISO security divisions establish and maintain contact with relevant Government and
commercial groups and associations within the security community, including but not limited to the
United States Computer Emergency Readiness Team (US-CERT), US-CERT Government Forum of
Incident Response and Security Teams (GFIRST), National Institute of Standards and Technology
(NIST), SANS, International Information System Security Certification Consortium (ISC2), and FireEye.
These organizations/associations publish documents, reports, educational seminars, forums, and
training, which GSA personnel with systems security responsibility may utilize.

The GSA Privacy Office also maintains contact with relevant Government and commercial groups and
associations within the privacy community, including but not limited to the Federal Privacy Council,
NIST, MITRE and the International Association of Privacy Professionals (IAPP). These
organizations/associations publish documents, reports, educational seminars, forums, and training
which GSA personnel with privacy responsibility may utilize.

Participating in these groups and associations enables the security staff to maintain currency with
recommended security and privacy practices, techniques, and technologies. OCISO divisions may
attend seminars, conferences, vendor exhibits, attend training, and read various publications from
groups and associations within the privacy community to stay current with security-related
information such as threats, vulnerabilities, and incidents.

All noteworthy information obtained (e.g., threats, vulnerabilities, incidents) is shared with
appropriate agency stakeholders within GSA to facilitate security awareness.

implemented-requirements.description:
GSA OCISO manages GSA’s Threat Awareness Program, as described in [CIO-IT Security-01-02](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): Incident Response
(IR). GSA OCISO reviews indicators of compromise (e.g., domains/Internet Protocol (IP) addresses of known
malicious actors, hashes of malicious files, traffic excerpts of suspicious activity) from threat intelligence for
actionable information and shares this information with relevant System Owners, United States Computer
Emergency Readiness Team (US-CERT), and other government agencies as needed. US-CERT coordinates
communication of threat intelligence information between GSA and other Federal agencies. GSA OCISO
implements proactive blocking of IP addresses, Uniform Resource Locators (URLs), hashes, and fraudulent email
senders, as necessary. Additional details regarding threat sources and the sharing of information are contained
in CIO-IT Security-01-02.

On September 21, 2022, GSA’s OCSIO Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation (CDM) Dashboard became the first
external agency to exchange “object-level data” with Cybersecurity Infrastructure Security Agency’s (CISA) CDM
Federal Dashboard. The automated data exchange achieved between the agency’s dashboards enables the
sharing of GSA’s threat intelligence data with CISA.

statements.description:
Pursuant to [GSA Order CIO 2103.2](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Policy,” GSA has
established a CUI Program Office and has disseminated associated program procedures for ensuring
the requirements of the protections of CUI data processed, stored, or transmitted on GSA external
facing systems, are implemented in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives,
policies, regulations, and standards.

The GSA CUI Program Office reviews and updates CIO 2103.2 and associated procedures at least
every three (3) years and following any changes to Federal or GSA policies, requirements, or
guidance.

[CIO-IT Privacy-23-01](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/security-and-privacy/privacy): Privacy Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Processing and Transparency
(PT) provides a comprehensive approach for managing privacy risks associated with GSA information
systems that contain PII data in accordance with Federal laws, regulations, and requirements.

The GSA Privacy Office updates CIO-IT Privacy-23-01 at least every three (3) years and following
changes to Federal or GSA policies, requirements, or guidance.

implemented-requirements.description:
GSA has a designated Chief Privacy Officer (CPO) and Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP) who have the
authority to allocate sufficient resources to implement and operate the organization-wide privacy program. The
CPO leads the GSA Privacy Office which develops privacy policies and manages the [GSA Privacy Program](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/security-and-privacy/privacy).

statements.description:
GSA privacy practices are publicly available at the [GSA Privacy Program](https://www.gsa.gov/reference/gsa-privacy-program/) web page. The GSA Privacy
Office manages these resources, providing the public with access to information about GSA’s privacy
activities and the ability to communicate with GSA’s Chief Privacy Officer (CPO).

GSA privacy practices are publicly available at the [GSA Privacy Program](https://www.gsa.gov/reference/gsa-privacy-program/) web page. The GSA Privacy
Office manages the publicly available privacy resources ensuring its practices and reports are publicly
available.

GSA privacy practices are publicly available at the [GSA Privacy Program](https://www.gsa.gov/reference/gsa-privacy-program/) web page. The GSA Privacy
Office manages these resources to include the GSA Privacy Office email address
(privacy.office@gsa.gov). This enables the public to provide feedback and/or submit questions about
privacy practices directly to the CPO.

implemented-requirements.description:
GSA privacy practices are publicly available at the [GSA Privacy Program](https://www.gsa.gov/reference/gsa-privacy-program/) web page. The GSA Privacy Act Rules
provide the public with access to information about GSA privacy activities and the ability to communicate with
GSA’s Chief Privacy Officer. More information regarding dissemination of privacy program information can be
found in [41 CFR Part 105-64](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-41/subtitle-C/chapter-105/part-105-64).

1. The GSA Privacy Program information provided on the [GSA Privacy Program](https://www.gsa.gov/reference/gsa-privacy-program/) web page is written in plain
language and organized in a way that is easy to understand and navigate.
1. Information required by the public to make an informed decision about whether and how to interact with
GSA Privacy Program is available; and
1. The online privacy practices are updated whenever GSA makes a substantive change to the practices.
Changes include a time/date stamp to inform the public when the most recent changes were made.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners are responsible for maintaining
an accurate accounting of disclosures of PII held in each system of records.

statements.description:
The GSA Privacy Office supports System Owners, who are responsible for maintaining an accurate
accounting of disclosures of PII held in each system of records under its control including date,
nature, and purpose of each disclosure of a record and the name and address of the person or
agency to which the disclosure was made.

The GSA Privacy Office supports System Owners, who are responsible for retaining the accounting of
disclosures for the life of the record or five years after the disclosure is made (whichever is longer).
Per the National Archives and Records Administration [General Records Schedule 4.2](https://www.archives.gov/files/records-mgmt/grs/grs04-2.pdf),
“Information Access and Protection Records” Item 50, which covers part a of the control described above, GSA
System Owners are asked to retain the following for each disclosure:

* Forms with the subject individual's name
* Records of the requester's name and address
* Explanations of the purpose for the request
* Date of disclosure
* Proof of subject individual's consent

Systems owners are notified of this specific retention issue. All GSA employees complete records
management training each year and are provided with resources for assistance, when needed.

The GSA Privacy Office supports System Owners, who are responsible for making the accounting of
disclosures available to the individual named in the record upon request.

The GSA Privacy Office develops privacy policies and manages the Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA)
template. The GSA privacy program policies and accompanying GSA requirements for PIAs ensure
that the highest quality of data protection for PII is used and is in accordance with applicable laws
and NIST recommendations. GSA system owners are responsible for confirming, to the greatest
extent practicable, the accuracy, relevance, timeliness, and completeness of that information. The
PIA prompts system owners to describe the source of the data and any technical solutions, policies,
or procedures focused on data accuracy and integrity of the project. GSA’s Privacy Office strives to
collect PII directly from the individual to the greatest extent practicable.

The GSA Privacy Office supports System Owners, who are responsible for checking for and correcting
as necessary any inaccurate or outdated PII. The Privacy Office issues guidelines aimed at ensuring
and maximizing the quality, utility, objectivity, and integrity of disseminated information.

The GSA Privacy Office supports System Owners, who are responsible for disseminating notice of
corrected or deleted PII to individuals or other appropriate entities. The GSA Privacy Office can
provide technical assistance or guidance as needed.

The GSA Privacy Office hears appeals of adverse decisions on correction or deletion requests in
accordance with [41 C.F.R. Part 105-64](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-41/subtitle-C/chapter-105/part-105-64) - GSA PRIVACY ACT RULES.

implemented-requirements.description:
GSA has established a data governance body documented by the GSA Evidence-Based Data Governance
Executive Board (EDGE) charter. The EDGE Board serves as a decisional board on Agency data and will advise
executive leadership on how to promote and invest in the use of Federal data for evidence building (i.e., data
governance). The Board oversees and promotes the Agency implementation of laws, policies, and regulations
related to data governance as required by the statute and implementing guidance. The EDGE Board is co-
chaired by the Deputy Administrator and GSA’s Chief Data Officer (CDO) and will undertake activities necessary
to carry out its responsibilities under the [Evidence Act](https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/house-bill/4174).

statements.description:
GSA is not currently a party to any Computer Matching Agreements. However, if required, the GSA
Data Integrity Board, headed by the Senior Agency Official for Privacy, oversees organizational
Computer Matching Agreements and would review proposals to conduct or participate in a matching
program.

GSA is not currently a party to any Computer Matching Agreements. However, if required, the GSA
Data Integrity Board, headed by the Senior Agency Official for Privacy, oversees organizational
Computer Matching Agreements and would review proposals to conduct or participate in a matching
program and thereafter would conduct annual reviews of all matching programs in which GSA has
participated.

GSA IT Security Policy and GSA requirements for Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), System of
Records Notices (SORN), Privacy Act Statements, and Annual Reviews of system notices ensure that
GSA identifies the minimum Personally Identifiable Information (PII) elements that are relevant and
necessary to accomplish the legally authorized purpose of collection.

The GSA IT Security Policy and GSA requirements for PIAs, SORNs, Privacy Act Statements, and
Annual Reviews of system notices ensure that the collection and retention of PII is limited to the
minimum elements identified for the purposes described in the notice for which the individual has
provided consent.

The GSA Privacy Office conducts an initial evaluation of PII holdings and establishes and follows a
schedule for regularly reviewing those holdings annually to ensure that only PII identified in the
notice is collected and retained and that the PII continues to be necessary to accomplish the legally
authorized purpose.

The GSA Privacy Office annually reviews and updates the GSA Privacy Program’s policies and
procedures to minimize the usage of PII throughout the agency.

The GSA Privacy Office develops privacy policies and manages the GSA privacy program. GSA
maintains a dedicated email account for receiving and responding to complaints, concerns, or
questions from individuals about the organization's privacy practices. Detailed information about
GSA PII complaint management can be found in [CFR Part 105-64](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-41/subtitle-C/chapter-105/part-105-64), “GSA Privacy Act Rules” and on the
[GSA Privacy Program](https://www.gsa.gov/reference/gsa-privacy-program/) web page.

Information necessary for filing a GSA Privacy Act Request (or complaint) is available on GSA’s
[Privacy Act of 1974](https://www.gsa.gov/reference/gsa-privacy-program/privacy-act-of-1974) web page.

The GSA Privacy Office utilizes a shared Privacy Office email (privacy.office@gsa.gov) inbox for
tracking all received complaints. The shared inbox ensures each complaint is reviewed and addressed
within 30 days.

The GSA Privacy Office acknowledges receipt of complaints, concerns, or questions from individuals
within 60 days of acquiring their email.

The GSA Privacy Office responds to complaints, concerns, or questions from individuals within 90
days of receiving their email.

The GSA Privacy Office develops, disseminates, and updates the annual Senior Agency Official for
Privacy (SAOP) FISMA report and works with other program offices on quarterly Federal Information
Security Modernization Act (FISMA) reports in response to the Office of Management and Budget
(OMB), Congress, and other oversight bodies, as appropriate to demonstrate accountability with
specific statutory and regulatory privacy program mandates, and to senior management and other
personnel with responsibility for monitoring privacy program progress and compliance.
The GSA Privacy Office reviews and updates the agency’s privacy reports annually.

GSA IT has established an Enterprise Risk and Strategic Initiatives (ERSI) board for strengthening Risk
Management at GSA. The ERSI Board serves as the governance body for translating enterprise-level
risk strategies into actionable initiatives and implementing sound risk management principles across
GSA functions and programs. Key activities of the ERSI board include but are not limited to:

1. Risk Prioritization and Development of Enterprise Risk Profiles: Identify and prioritize the
most significant enterprise risks to GSA’s mission for consideration by leadership.
2. Risk Mitigation: Establish risk owners for enterprise-wide threats and work with them to
develop and implement mitigation actions.
3. Monitoring and Communication: Review and monitor the effectiveness of mitigation
strategies and regularly exchange information to improve leadership understanding about
ongoing risk actions.
4. Decision Support: Bring Agency leaders together to integrate risk management practices
into strategic planning and resource allocation.
5. Problem Solving: Leverage the experience of a diverse cross-functional team to critically
think through strategic challenges and opportunities and provide solutions.
6. Transparency and Accountability: Foster transparency and clear accountability for
enterprise risks while embedding the tenets of effective risk management into GSA’s
culture.

The risk framing results are distributed to the Co-Chaired by Deputies, Performance Improvement
Officer (PIO) and Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) with “Risk Leads” from major Services and
Staff Offices (SSOs), as well as the Chief Data Officer (CDO), Chief Privacy Officer, Evaluation Officer,
and A-Suite Representative.

The GSA IT ERSI board performs risk framing activities annually and as needed to identify, validate,
and prioritize the most significant enterprise risks to GSA and for ensuring risk owners are effectively
executing mitigation activities as assigned.

The GSA IT Enterprise Risk and Strategic Initiatives (ERSI) Board is Co-Chaired by the Deputy
Performance Improvement Officer (PIO) and Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) for aligning
GSA’s information security and privacy management processes with strategic, operational, and
budgetary planning processes.

The key activities performed by the ERSI board address identifying and documenting risk
assumptions, constraints, priorities, and organizational risk tolerance. The ERSI board has defined the
steps of GSA’s Risk framework as Identify, Assess, Analyze and Prioritize, Manage and Escalate, and
Implement and Monitor with Communication being central at all stages. The ERSI board also defines
GSA’s Risk profile for submission to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB).

GSA has documented its organization-wide supply chain risk management strategy procedures in
[CIO-IT Security-21-117](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): OCISO Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) Program and
[CIO-IT Security-Privacy-18-90](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): Common Control Catalog (CCC). The procedures facilitate implementation of
the supply chain risk management policy and associated controls.

Supply chain risk management procedures for GSA IT managed information systems are defined and
documented within CIO-IT Security-21-117. The guide serves as the Tier 2 (organizational) plan for
GSA IT in accordance with [NIST SP 800-161, Revision 1](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-161r1.pdf), “Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk
Management Practices for Systems and Organizations.” The guide identifies how the OCISO C-SCRM
Program within the ICAM Shared Services Division (ISI) of GSA IT manages supplier induced
information security risks for GSA IT systems throughout their lifecycle, including pre-award
mitigations and post-award monitoring of risks. The C-SCRM Program’s operational activities are
supported by Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that detail how the program activities are
executed.

CIO-IT Security-21-117 is reviewed/updated annually upon changes to Federal or GSA policies
requirements or guidance. ISI ensures the program’s SOPs are updated annually.

implemented-requirements.description:
The OCISO C-SCRM team develops, maintains, and annually updates a list of critical suppliers for GSA IT. The list
is based on input from various sources for GSA-IT managed systems and includes software inventories,
hardware inventories, and financials related to acquisitions. Supply chain risks that are unique for the most
critical vendors are then incorporated into final determinations. Supplier assessments are conducted for the
resultant set of critical vendors, and significant risks are addressed. The specific controls for maintaining the
critical supplier list and conducting supplier reviews are identified within the C-SCRM Program’s SOPs.

statements.description:
The GSA OCISO has developed [CIO-IT Security-12-66](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): Information Security Continuous Monitoring
(ISCM) Strategy & Ongoing Authorization (OA) Program and has established system-level metric
monitoring requirements, as defined by Section 3 of [CIO-IT Security-08-39](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): IT Security Program
Management Implementation Plan.

The GSA OCISO has established system-level monitoring and control assessment requirements within
CIO-IT Security-08-39 and CIO-IT Security-12-66.

The GSA OCISO performs ongoing monitoring of system and organization-defined metrics using
automated enterprise management tools and manual processes defined by:

* CIO-IT Security-06-30: Managing Enterprise Risk
* CIO-IT Security-08-39: IT Security Program Management Implementation Plan
* CIO-IT Security-09-44: Plan of Action and Milestones
* CIO-IT Security-17-80: Vulnerability Management Process
* CIO-IT Security-18-91: Risk Management Strategy (RMS)
* CIO-IT Security-19-101: External Information System Monitoring

The OCISO performs POA&M reviews upon completion of an A&A and quarterly thereafter. System
Level Quarterly POA&M Review Reports are generated by the OCSIO and are provided to ISSOs for
quality reviews and process improvement activities. ISSM Management Reports are generated
quarterly by the OCISO for providing an agency view of status in correcting weaknesses or
deficiencies associated with the managed information system portfolio.

The OCISO has established and defined system-level response action requirements within:

* CIO-IT Security-06-30: Managing Enterprise Risk
* CIO-IT Security-09-44: Plan of Action and Milestones
* CIO-IT Security-17-80: Vulnerability Management Process

The OCISO has established and defined methods for reporting System-Level security and privacy
status within the CIO-IT Security-08-39 and CIO-IT Security-12-66. The OCISO conducts quarterly
AO/CISO briefings during which systems’ cyber hygiene and operational statuses are reported to the
AOs.

implemented-requirements.description:
GSA has defined 16 Mission Essential functions (MEFs) and Essential Supporting Activities (ESAs) across GSA
Service and Staff Offices (SSOs). More information on GSA MEFs is available in [GSA Order ADM 2430.2](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “The
U.S. General Services Administration Continuity of Operations Mission Essential Functions.” GSA Office of
Mission Assurance (OMA), per ADM 2430.2, reviews GSA MEFs and PMEFs on a biennial basis. Correspondingly,
GSA information systems supporting these MEFs are also updated.

statements.description:
1. The GSA personnel security policy is defined in the GSA Order CIO 2100.1, “GSA Information Technology (IT) Security Policy,” GSA Order ADM 9732.1,
“Personnel Security and Suitability Program Handbook” and GSA Order ADM 2181.1,
“Homeland Security Presidential Directive-12, Personal Identity Verification and Credentialing, and Background Investigations for Contractors.”
which address purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination
among organizational entities, and compliance for personnel security activities. These policies
are consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards,
and guidelines. These policies are disseminated GSA-wide via GSA’s InSite centralized agency
[Directives website](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library).
2. Personnel security procedures are documented in CIO-IT Security-03-23: Termination and
Transfer and in CIO-IT Security-Privacy-18-90: Common Control Catalog (CCC). These procedures
facilitate the implementation of the personnel security policy and associated controls. These
guides are disseminated GSA-wide via GSA’s InSite centralized agency
[IT Security Procedural Guides website](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides).

Per 2100.1, the CISO is responsible for managing the development and publishing of all security
policies and IT security procedural guides.

The GSA OCISO is responsible for reviewing and updating:

1. CIO 2100.1 annually and following changes to Federal or GSA policies, requirements, or
guidance.
2. CIO-IT Security-03-23 every three years and following changes to Federal or GSA policies,
requirements, or guidance.

[GSA Order ADM 9732.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “Personnel Security and Suitability Program Handbook” describes the
process GSA uses to designate the risk levels for positions in GSA.

ADM 9732.1 provides the screening criteria (i.e., requirements for investigations, suitability
adjudications, and security clearance determinations for GSA employees). Requirements for
contractors are contained in [GSA Order ADM 2181.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “Homeland Security Presidential Directive-12,
Personal Identity Verification and Credentialing, and Background Investigations for Contractors,” and
[GSA Order ADM 5400.2](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “General Services Administration Heads of Services and Staff Offices’ and
Requesting Officials’ Roles and Responsibilities to Implement Homeland Security Presidential Directive-12.”

GSA position risk designations are reviewed and updated, as necessary, to meet changing roles,
responsibilities, and Federal requirements.

[GSA Order CIO 2100.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “GSA Information Technology (IT) Security Policy,” requires an initial fitness
determination as part of the background investigation process prior to users being granted access to
the GSA network and GSA IT systems. [GSA Order ADM 9732.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “Personnel Security and Suitability
Program Handbook” provides the screening criteria (e.g., requirements for investigations, suitability
adjudications, and security clearance determinations for GSA employees). [GSA Order ADM 2181.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library),
“Homeland Security Presidential Directive-12, Personal Identity Verification and Credentialing, and
Background Investigations for Contractors” provides screening criteria and access to IT systems
guidelines for contractors.

ADM 9732.1 provides the re-screening criteria (i.e., number of years between investigations) for GSA
employees. For contractors, ADM 2181.1 states that it must be used in conjunction with ADM 9732.1
which identifies the time periods for rescreening of individuals.

implemented-requirements.description:
**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** The GSA supervisor/CO/COR is responsible for notifying the appropriate
System Owner/Account Manager about a user’s off-boarding so they can take appropriate action at a
system/application level. The GSA supervisor/CO/COR is responsible for submitting a GSA off-boarding
ServiceNow ticket required per assigned personnel.

statements.description:
Disabling GSA account(s)/information system access is initiated and facilitated by an individual’s
supervisor/Contracting Officer (CO)/Contracting Officer Representative (COR). GSA account access
(ENT Long-Name Account [LNA] and Short-Name Account [SNA]) is disabled within 24 hours of an
approved Service Catalog Request indicating personnel termination.

Terminating/revoking of all information system-related property which includes HSPD-12 cards,
authentication tokens (USB for privileged access), laptops, etc. is facilitated by the supervisor and
sent to GSA IT support personnel based on the Service Catalog Request.

Exit interviews are initiated and facilitated by the supervisor/CO/COR of an individual ensuring that
privacy, disclosure, and confidentiality responsibilities are reviewed with the person leaving.

Retrieval of all information system-related property which includes HSPD-12 cards, authentication
tokens (USB for privileged access), laptops, etc. is facilitated by the supervisor and sent to GSA IT
support personnel based on the Service Catalog Request.

As part of user off-boarding, the supervisor/CO/COR is responsible for coordinating with GSA IT
support personnel the transfer of organizational information and information systems based on the
Service Catalog Request.

implemented-requirements.description:
**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** Supervisors/CO/COR are responsible for notifying the appropriate System
Owner/Account Manager of a user’s transfer so they can take appropriate action at a system/application level.

statements.description:
Review of an individual’s ongoing operational need for current logical and physical access is initiated
and facilitated by the individual’s supervisor/ Contracting Officer (CO)/Contracting Officer
Representative (COR). The supervisor/CO/COR is responsible for initiating transfer procedures (with
the individual), such as creating a Service Catalog Request, as necessary, to ensure the user’s access
is adjusted as appropriate for their new assignment. For additional details, refer to
[CIO-IT Security-03-23](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): Termination and Transfer.

Access is denied or modified within 3 days of an approved Service Catalog Request indicating
personnel transfer.

The supervisor/CO/COR is responsible for coordinating with the user to ensure modifications to the
user’s access, as appropriate, to their new assignment. If necessary, Service Catalog Request(s) can
be opened to facilitate access modifications.

Supervisors are notified within 24 hours that a personnel transfer Service Catalog Request has been
serviced.

implemented-requirements.description:
**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** If a managed system does not have system
specific access agreement requirements, the System Owner may leverage the OCISO PS-6 control response as a
Common Control.

If a managed system has specific or unique access agreement requirements identified, the System Owner is
responsible for ensuring the unique access agreement is documented and is acknowledged in conjunction with
GSA’s access agreement for meeting the system’s specific access and usage requirements, making the control
Hybrid. Additional system-specific portions of the control are reviewing and updating the system’s unique
access agreement and documenting acknowledgment of it.

Any unique access agreement required by a system, a Service, or a Staff Organization must comply with GSA’s IT
Rules of Behavior (refer to PL-4 guidance).

statements.description:
GSA has developed a common access agreement (i.e., “GSA IT Rules of Behavior for General Users”)
as indicated in [CIO-IT Security-05-29](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides): Security and Privacy Awareness and Role Based Training
Program.
GSA OCISO reviews and updates the GSA IT Rules of Behavior for General Users annually.

1. All GSA IT users must sign the GSA IT General Rules of Behavior for General Users within 90 days
of their entry on duty (EoD).
2. All GSA IT users are required to re-sign the GSA IT Rules of Behavior for General Users annually
as part of GSA’s annual IT Security and Privacy Awareness training.

implemented-requirements.description:
**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners must ensure all external provider contracts include GSA’s
third party personnel security requirements.

statements.description:
All third-party personnel (i.e., Vendors/Contractors) providing services or equipment to GSA must
adhere to [GSA Order CIO 2100.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “GSA Information Technology (IT) Security Policy,” regarding
security roles and responsibilities and personnel security requirements.

All third parties must comply with CIO 2100.1, [GSA Order ADM 2181.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “Homeland Security Presidential Directive-12,
Personal Identity Verification and Credentialing, and Background Investigations for Contractors,”
[GSA Order ADM 9732.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “Personnel Security and Suitability Program Handbook,” and
[GSA Order ADM 5400.2](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library), “General Services Administration Heads of Services and
Staff Offices’ and Requesting Officials’ Roles and Responsibilities to Implement Homeland Security
Presidential Directive-12.”

GSA’s personnel security requirements are documented in CIO 2100.1, ADM 2181.1, ADM 9732.1,
and ADM 5400.2.

CIO 2100.1 and [CIO-IT Security-03-23](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/it-security-and-privacy/it-security/it-security-procedural-guides):
Termination and Transfer require supervisors to notify the
appropriate personnel of any personnel transfers or terminations within 3 business days.
GSA monitors third party compliance via contractual requirements and identification of inactive accounts.

GSA Federal personnel are subject to sanctions as described in [GSA Order HRM 9751.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library),
“Maintaining Discipline” regarding delinquency or misconduct, including security violations.

Supervisors, after coordinating with the servicing human resources office, must notify appropriate
personnel within three days when a formal sanctions process is initiated, including identifying the
individual and reason for the sanction if approved by the human resources office.

implemented-requirements.description:
Security and privacy roles and responsibilities and position descriptions are defined within
[GSA Order CIO 2100.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library) “GSA Information Technology (IT) Security Policy” and
[GSA Order CIO 2200.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library) “GSA Privacy Act Program.”

statements.description:
1. The GSA Privacy Office develops, disseminates, and implements operational privacy policies that
govern the appropriate privacy and security controls for programs, information systems, or
technologies involving PII. They are disseminated via the [Privacy InSite page](https://insite.gsa.gov/employee-resources/information-technology/security-and-privacy/privacy).

a. The policies and procedures on the Privacy page address purpose, scope, roles,
responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and
compliance.
b. The Privacy policies, procedures, and processes are consistent with Federal laws, orders,
directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.

2. The GSA Privacy Office develops, disseminates, and implements operational privacy procedures
(e.g., Privacy Threshold Assessment [PTA] and Privacy Impact Assessment [PIA] processes) via
the Privacy InSite page that provide guidance for processing PII and complying with associated
privacy controls.

GSA has a designated Chief Privacy Officer (CPO) and a Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP) and
allocates sufficient resources to implement and operate the organization-wide privacy program. The
CPO leads the GSA Privacy Office which develops privacy policies and manages the GSA Privacy
Program.

1. The GSA Privacy Office develops, disseminates, and implements operational privacy policies that
govern the appropriate privacy and security controls for programs, information systems, or
technologies involving PII in accordance with Federal laws, policies, and requirements. They are
reviewed on an annual basis and updated as necessary.
2. The GSA Privacy Office develops, disseminates, and implements operational privacy procedures
(e.g., PTA and PIA processes) that provide guidance for identifying and safeguarding Personally
Identifiable Information (PII). They are reviewed on an annual basis and updated as necessary.

implemented-requirements.description:
**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners and Data Owners are responsible
for determining and documenting the legal authority permitting the handling of PII data within a SORN,
pursuant to [5 U.S.C. §552a (e) (3)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2021-title5/pdf/USCODE-2021-title5-partI-chap5-subchapII-sec552a.pdf).
When drafting a Privacy Act Statement for review by the GSA Privacy Office,
the System Owner must include the legal authority for collecting the information. System Owners are
responsible for ensuring only authorized Personally Identifiable Information (PII) data is processed by the
system per its documented SORN.

statements.description:
The GSA Privacy Office provides guidance and oversight to System Owners and Data Owners in
documenting their Privacy Act Systems of Records Notices (SORN). The standard format of the GSA
SORN requires the identification of the specific authority that permits the processing of the
personally identifiable information.

The individual must provide information to verify eligibility to access controlled systems or facilities.
All collections are voluntary. Collections may be listed as “mandatory” only if the person is required
by law to provide the data AND the person is subject to a penalty for refusing. Only the minimum
required information is collected in order to provide access.

implemented-requirements.description:
**Federal System-Specific Control Expectation:**

a. When drafting a Privacy Act Statement for review by the GSA Privacy Office, the System Owner must
include the purpose(s) for collecting the information.
c. The System Owner is responsible for ensuring that PII is shared only for the authorized purpose(s)
identified in the Privacy Act and/or in public notices.
d. The System Owner is responsible for ensuring that the annual PIA updates are made in coordination with
the ISSO or that if there are no significant changes to the PII in the system, that the PIA is recertified.

statements.description:
The GSA Privacy Office provides guidance and oversight to System Owners in documenting their
Privacy Act Systems of Records Notices (SORN). The standard format of the GSA SORN requires the
identification of the purpose for processing of the personally identifiable information.

The GSA Privacy Office develops privacy policies and manages the GSA Privacy Program. The GSA
privacy training and the GSA requirements for Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) and SORNs ensure
that GSA uses Personally Identifiable Information (PII) internally only for the authorized purpose(s)
identified in the Privacy Act and/or in public notices.

The GSA Privacy Office develops and collaborates with necessary Services and Staff Offices (SSOs) to
develop privacy policies and manage the GSA Privacy Program. [GSA Order CIO 2180.2](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library),
“GSA Rules of Behavior for Handling Personally Identifiable Information (PII),” and within [GSA Order CIO 2100.1](https://insite.gsa.gov/directives-library)
“GSA Information Technology (IT) Security Policy,” ensure that GSA is in accordance with applicable
laws and National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) recommendations for sharing
information with third parties. Personal information used to determine employee rights, benefits,
and privileges is collected directly from the individual of record whenever possible and used only for
the purpose for which it is intended. Each system of records manager must set up technical,
administrative, and physical security measures for processing, storing, transmitting, and disposing of
information in the system. All employees who work with a system's information as part of their job
must follow these measures. Security measures for paper records include storage in secure cabinets
or rooms, with access limited to authorized personnel. Electronic records are protected by
passwords, firewalls, and other administrative, technical, and physical security measures determined
to be necessary by the system manager and program officials, pursuant to [5 U.S.C. §552a (e) (10)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2021-title5/pdf/USCODE-2021-title5-partI-chap5-subchapII-sec552a.pdf).

The Information System Security Officer (ISSO) is responsible for coordinating the annual review and
updating the system/application PIA in GSA’s Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) system/tool
(currently Archer). PIAs must be updated when there are significant changes and are required to
receive stakeholder approvals. SORNs must be updated whenever there is a significant change.

implemented-requirements.description:
The GSA Privacy Office develops privacy policies and manages the GSA privacy program which provides a
means, where feasible and appropriate, for individuals to authorize the collection, use, maintaining, and sharing
of personally identifiable information (PII) prior to its collection.

GSA Orders CIO 1878.3, “Developing and Maintaining Privacy Threshold Assessments, Privacy Impact
Assessments, Privacy Act Notices, and System of Records Notices,” and CIO 2180.2, “GSA Rules of Behavior for
Handling Personally Identifiable Information (PII)” provide appropriate means for individuals to understand the
consequences of decisions to approve or decline the authorization of the collection, use, dissemination, and
retention of PII.

The GSA Privacy Office advises the System Owner on how to obtain consent, where feasible and appropriate,
from individuals prior to any new uses or disclosure of previously collected PII.

The GSA Privacy Act Program ensures that individuals are aware of and, where feasible, consent to all uses of PII
not initially described in the public notice that was in effect at the time the organization collected the PII.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners are responsible for adding
Privacy Act Statements to their systems at the point of data collection.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners are responsible for coordinating
with the Privacy Program to ensure individuals have the ability to access their PII in accordance with GSA
policies and procedures. Additionally, System Owners are responsible for coordinating with the Privacy Program
to ensure privacy notices and the rights of individuals are accurate and kept current.

statements.description:
GSA complies with the [Plain Writing Act of 2010](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-111publ274/pdf/PLAW-111publ274.pdf) which requires all federal agencies to write "clear
government communication that the public can understand and use."

GSA adheres to [Privacy Act of 1974](https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/USCODE-2010-title5/pdf/USCODE-2010-title5-partI-chap5-subchapII-sec552a.pdf) requirements and Office of Management and Budget (OMB)
policies and guidance for the proper processing of Privacy Act Requests.

The GSA Privacy Program provides templates and guidance on how to describe: 1) the PII the
organization collects and the purpose(s) for which it collects that information; 2) how the
organization uses PII internally; 3) whether the organization shares PII with external entities and the
categories of those entities and the purposes for such sharing; 4) whether individuals have the ability
to consent to specific uses or sharing of PII and how to exercise any such consent; 5) how individuals
may obtain access to PII; and 6) how the PII is protected.

Personal information used to determine employee rights, benefits, and privileges must be collected
directly from the individual of record whenever possible and used only for the purpose for which it is
intended. If the information needs to come from a third party, the individual's written permission is
required. Statutory authority must exist for collecting Social Security Numbers (SSNs) for record
systems that use the SSN for identification purposes. SSNs are not to be collected for systems
without this specific authority.

SSNs are not to be collected for systems that were established under a statutory authority in effect
before January 1, 1975. Systems that were established before January 1, 1975, must be revised to
avoid the collection and use of the SSNs.

The term “Personally Identifiable Information,” as defined in [OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf),
“Managing Information as a Strategic Resource,” means information that can be used to distinguish or trace an
individual’s identity, either alone or when combined with other information that is linked or linkable
to a specific individual.”

implemented-requirements.description:
The GSA Privacy Office and System Owners include Privacy Act Statements on GSA forms that collect Personally
Identifiable Information (PII).

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners are responsible for coordinating
with the GSA Privacy Program to ensure System of Record Notices (SORNs) and Privacy Act notices on forms
that collect PII are kept current.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners are responsible for coordinating
with the GSA Privacy Program and Regulatory Secretariat Division to ensure SORNs and Privacy Act notices on
forms that collect PII are kept current.

If a significant alteration needs to be made to a system of records, GSA amends the existing SORN for that
system of records and republish it in the Federal Register to comply with the OMB requirements in
[OMB Circular A-108](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A108/omb_circular_a-108.pdf), “Federal Agency Responsibilities for Review, Reporting, and Publication under the Privacy Act.”

statements.description:
Office of Management and Budget (OMB) [Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf) Appendix I, “Responsibilities for Protecting
and Managing Federal Information Resource,” serves as the baseline for distinguishing between the
criteria for drafting a new SORN versus amending an existing SORN. A “new” system of records is one
for which no public notice is currently published in the Federal Register. A new SORN must be
published when any one of the following criteria is met:

* A program, authorized by a new or existing statute or Executive order (EO), maintains
information on an individual and retrieves that information by personal identifier.
* There is a new organization of records resulting in the consolidation of two or more existing
systems into one new umbrella system, whenever the consolidation cannot be classified
under a current SORN.
* It is discovered that records about individuals are being created and used, and that this
activity is not covered by a currently published SORN. In this case, OMB requires the
temporary suspension of data collection and disclosure.
* A new organization (configuration) of existing records about individuals that was not
previously subject to the Privacy Act (i.e., was not a system of records) results in the
creation of a system of records.

The GSA Privacy Office publishes System of Records Notices (SORNs) in the Federal Register, subject
to required oversight processes, for systems containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
When a GSA organization proposes to establish a new system of records or significantly revise an
existing one, the program manager notifies the GSA Privacy Act Officer, which helps in preparing a
SORN using the prescribed format, coordinate its review and approval within GSA, and submit it for
evaluation by OMB and Congress and for publication in the Federal Register.

The GSA Privacy Office and System Owners keep SORNs current, perform an annual review of SORNs,
and include Privacy Act Statements on GSA forms that collect PII. More information regarding System
of Records Notices and Privacy Act Statements can be found in [41 CFR Part 105-64](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2010-title41-vol3/pdf/CFR-2010-title41-vol3-sec105-64-108.pdf).

implemented-requirements.description:
Routine uses apply to information sharing external to GSA. The term “routine use” is defined, with respect to
the disclosure of a record, as “the use of such a record for a purpose which is compatible with the purpose for
which the record was collected.” This section describes each situation in which GSA may share records on
individuals covered by the SORN under the Privacy Act Section 552a(b)(3). The routine uses must be compatible
and consistent with the purpose for which the record was collected. This ensures the public receives adequate
notice of the agency’s planned uses of the information in the system of records. The following language must be
included prior to the list of routine uses: “In addition to those disclosures generally permitted under 5 U.S.C.
552a(b) of the Privacy Act, all or a portion of the records or information contained in this system may be
disclosed to authorized entities, as is determined to be relevant and necessary, outside GSA as a routine use
pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 552a(b)(3) as follows:”

Common routine uses for most systems of records include sharing.

* For audits and oversight.
* For congressional inquiries.
* With contractors, grantees, and experts to perform OPM-authorized activities.
* For investigations of potential violations of law.
* For intelligence purposes.
* With the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) for records management purposes.
* For litigation purposes.
* For data breach and mitigation response.

SORNS must be updated whenever there is a significant change.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners and Data Owners are responsible
for coordinating with the GSA Privacy Program to ensure SORNs and Privacy Act notices on forms that collect
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) are kept current.

The Privacy Act requires that a notice describing each System of Records proposed for establishment be
published in the Federal Register for review and comment by the public and other interested parties. The notice
allows questions to be raised and resolved before the system is put into effect and ensures that privacy
considerations have been addressed. GSA complies with the Privacy Act requirements.

There are no exceptions to the SORN process. However, certain exemptions to the [Privacy Act of 1974](https://www.archives.gov/about/laws/privacy-act-1974.html) can be
claimed. The head of GSA may promulgate rules, in accordance with the requirements (including general notice)
of sections [U.S.C. 553](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2011-title5/pdf/USCODE-2011-title5-partI-chap5-subchapII-sec553.pdf)(b)(1), (2), and (3), (c), and (e) of this title, to exempt any system of records within the
agency from subsections (c)(3), (d), (e)(1), (e)(4)(G), (H), and (I) and (f) of this section.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners and Data Owners are responsible
for coordinating with the GSA Privacy Program to ensure that the agency promulgates any Privacy Act
exemption as a rule per GSA agency rulemaking procedures. At the time rules are adopted under this
subsection, GSA and/or its contractors shall include in the statement required under section 553(c) of the
Privacy Act, the reasons why the system of records is to be exempted from a provision of this section of the
Privacy Act. Any exemptions taken in a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking must be published as a Final Rule before
they are effective. Refer to OMB SORN Guidance in [Circular A-108](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A108/omb_circular_a-108.pdf),
“Federal Agency Responsibilities for Review, Reporting, and Publication under the Privacy Act” for
further information and specific criteria regarding submission of exemptions

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners and Data Owners are responsible
for eliminating unnecessary collection, maintenance, and use of SSNs, and explore alternatives to their use as a

Privacy Office, the System Owner must include the legal authority for collecting SSNs and why an alternative
cannot be used.

Under the [Privacy Act](https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/USCODE-2010-title5/pdf/USCODE-2010-title5-partI-chap5-subchapII-sec552a.pdf), 1677(a), agencies are prohibited from denying an individual any right, benefit,
or privilege provided by law because of the individual’s refusal to disclose his or her SSN unless
disclosure is required by federal statute.

Section 7(a)(1) of the Privacy Act (found at 5 U.S.C. § 552a note [Disclosure of Social Security
Number]) states, “It shall be unlawful for any Federal, State or local government agency to deny to
any individual any right, benefit, or privilege provided by law because of such individual’s refusal to
disclose his social security account number.” GSA is compliant with these regulations.

GSA Privacy Program supplies templates and guidance on to how provide effective notice to the
public and to individuals regarding: 1) its activities that impact privacy, including collection of social
security numbers; 2) whether that disclosure is mandatory or voluntary; 3) authority for collecting
social security number; and 4) how it will be used.

The GSA Privacy Office ensures that GSA uses Personally Identifiable Information (PII) internally only for the
authorized purpose(s) identified, and reviews processing activities to prohibit the processing of information
describing how an individual exercises rights guaranteed by the First Amendment unless expressly authorized by
statute or by the individual or unless pertinent to and within the scope of an authorized law enforcement
activity.

**Federal System-Specific Expectation:** System Owners are responsible for coordinating
with the GSA Privacy Program to ensure that processing activities do not describe how an individual exercises
rights guaranteed by the First Amendment unless expressly authorized by statute or by the individual or unless
pertinent to and within the scope of an authorized law enforcement activity.

**Federal System-Specific Control Expectation:** System Owners must notify the GSA
Privacy Office in the event that GSA needs to establish a computer matching program or agreement to share
system of records information with other Federal or non-Federal agencies. A Data Integrity Board (DIB) will be
created to review and approve such programs and agreements.

The Computer Matching and Privacy Protection Act of 1988 (the Act), Pub.L.100-503, amends the Privacy Act of
1974, and establishes procedural safeguards affecting agencies' use of Privacy Act records in performing certain
types of computerized matching programs. The Act regulates the use of computer matching by federal agencies
involving personally identifiable records maintained in a system of records subject to the Privacy Act. The Act
requires agencies to have written agreements in place specifying the terms under which matches are to be
conducted. The Act applies to the computerized comparison of two or more automated systems of records (or
federal personnel or payroll systems of records) between federal agencies or between a federal agency and a
non-federal agency.

maintained in systems of records and incorporates the provisions of the Computer Matching and
Privacy Protection Act of 1988 ([Public Law 100-503](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-102/pdf/STATUTE-102-Pg2507.pdf#page=1)),
including the Computer Matching and Privacy Protection Amendments.

As defined by GSA’s SCRM Executive Board Charter, GSA has established a supply chain risk management team
consisting of SCRM Senior Accountable Officials who form GSA’s SCRM Executive Board. The board provides
oversight to any GSA SCRM working group(s) established to accomplish the following SCRM activities:

* Analyze GSA’s supply chain and use risk-based approaches to address supply chain risks (including, but
not limited to emerging risk information related to communications technology) to inform strategic
and operational management decisions and investments.
* Ensure policy development and resource management efforts include planning for and consideration
of incident management, contingency, continuity, and response requirements.
* Facilitate the coordinated alignment of GSA’s Government-wide responsibilities (e.g., policy, training,
shared services, interagency engagement, customer agency-facing service, product offerings, real
estate) with the internal GSA Enterprise responsibilities to safeguard and manage risk to GSA’s mission
and its portfolio of assets.
* Integrate SCRM policies, processes, and oversight activities into GSA’s internal acquisition processes
and information and communication technology (ICT) investment and lifecycle management processes.
* Provide guidance to internal GSA employees on supply chain risks and incorporate SCRM-relevant
responsibilities and duties, where applicable.
* Develop processes and procedures for supporting implementation of new statutory and regulatory
requirements related to SCRM.
* Develop processes and procedures for interfacing with external stakeholders on SCRM issues as
defined in the SCRM Executive Board Charter. Stakeholders include the Federal Acquisition Security
Council (FASC) Information Sharing, and Risk Management Task Force and the Department of
Homeland Security ICT SCRM Working Group.

The OCISO C-SCRM Team that exists within the ICAM Shared Services Division (ISI) serves as the C-SCRM Team
for all GSA IT systems.
